definition: A subset of data held out from training and used to tune hyperparameters and monitor model performance during development.
details: The validation set provides feedback for model-selection decisions without touching the final test set, helping avoid overfitting to the evaluation data itself.

explainer.lead: A validation set is a subset of data held out from training and used to tune hyperparameters and monitor performance during development. It matters because it guides model-selection decisions without contaminating the final evaluation.

tiers.eli5: It's a slice of data the model doesn't train on, used to check how it's doing while you're still building it.
tiers.practitioner: It provides feedback for model-selection decisions without touching the final test set. Pitfall: repeatedly tuning against it risks overfitting to the evaluation data itself.
tiers.paperLevel: A held-out subset used to tune hyperparameters and monitor model performance during development, helping avoid overfitting to the evaluation data.

explainer.example: A team adjusts regularisation strength based on validation-set scores, leaving the test set untouched until the end.
